plus1_left_out.outcome: missed: limit of the probe set

convention.note: fixture convention: each receiver owns one report lane and pulses its first frame's verdict as a width; not a chip feature
convention.time_zero: first clock lane 0's output enable is asserted

EdgeResync.algorithm: Single mid-bit sample that re-centres on every transition. A falling edge while idle starts a frame and schedules the start sample at T/2. Inside a frame, every transition of the line reschedules the next pending sample to the transition + T/2 (a transition on the clock a sample was due moves that sample; it is not taken first); after each sample the next is T later. Samples are start, eight data bits LSB first, stop. A high start sample is a false start (back to idle). The stop sample completes the frame and the receiver returns to idle.

LenientStop.algorithm: Single mid-bit sample with start validation and no stop check. A falling edge while idle starts a frame; the start sample at T/2 must be low, otherwise the receiver returns to idle. Data bits are sampled at T/2 + kT, LSB first. The stop bit's sample is taken at T/2 + 9T, which completes the frame, but its level is ignored: the frame always reports a high stop bit, so this receiver never reports a framing error.

Majority16.algorithm: Oversampling receiver: majority vote of three ticks around mid-bit. The line is looked at only on ticks, every T/ratio clocks, at tick phase p (ticks fall on the clocks where t mod (T/ratio) == p, t counted from the fixture's time zero). A frame starts at the first tick that reads low after a tick that read high, so the start edge is seen up to one tick late. Each bit's value is the majority of ticks ratio/2 - 1, ratio/2 and ratio/2 + 1 of that bit, counted from the detecting tick. A start bit whose majority is high is a false start: the receiver returns to idle. The stop bit is the tenth majority; the frame completes there and the receiver returns to idle. 16x oversampling: tick = T/16, vote of ticks 7, 8, 9 (clocks 14, 16, 18 at T=32). Algorithm as in _Majority: start edge seen at a tick, start-bit majority must be low or the receiver returns to idle, stop bit checked.

Majority8.algorithm: Oversampling receiver: majority vote of three ticks around mid-bit. The line is looked at only on ticks, every T/ratio clocks, at tick phase p (ticks fall on the clocks where t mod (T/ratio) == p, t counted from the fixture's time zero). A frame starts at the first tick that reads low after a tick that read high, so the start edge is seen up to one tick late. Each bit's value is the majority of ticks ratio/2 - 1, ratio/2 and ratio/2 + 1 of that bit, counted from the detecting tick. A start bit whose majority is high is a false start: the receiver returns to idle. The stop bit is the tenth majority; the frame completes there and the receiver returns to idle. 8x oversampling: tick = T/8, vote of ticks 3, 4, 5 (clocks 12, 16, 20 at T=32). Algorithm as in _Majority: start edge seen at a tick, start-bit majority must be low or the receiver returns to idle, stop bit checked.

MidSample.algorithm: Single sample at mid-bit, no start validation. Any falling edge while idle starts a frame. The line is sampled once per bit at T/2 + kT for k = 0..9 (start, eight data bits LSB first, stop); the start sample is not checked, so a glitch is accepted as a start bit. The frame completes at the stop sample and the receiver returns to idle, watching for the next falling edge.

MidSamplePlus1.algorithm: MidSample sampling one clock late: once per bit at T/2 + 1 + kT. Negative control for resolution. Everything else (no start validation, stop check, return to idle at the stop sample) is MidSample's.

MidSampleTwin.algorithm: MidSample's algorithm, written separately as a countdown state machine. A falling edge while idle loads a half-bit countdown; when it expires the line is sampled and the countdown reloads with a full bit. The first sample is the (unchecked) start bit, the next eight shift into the byte LSB first, and the tenth is the stop bit, which completes the frame and returns to idle. Negative control: it must land in MidSample's equivalence class.
